All set. Here's the "legend" playbook:

What changed in the pipeline

Identity is now one config file — twin.json. No more hardcoded names anywhere:
{"name": "Legend", "model": "legend"}
The parser auto-generates the matching Modelfile, and the exporter auto-names the output legend-v1.gguf.

On the new PC

1. Copy ai-twin-starter.zip from your Desktop → unzip anywhere
2. Install (order matters): NVIDIA driver → Ollama → wsl --install -d Ubuntu → run training/setup_wsl.sh in WSL → copy the .wslconfig settings (in REPLICATE.md)
3. Edit twin.json to Legend's name
4. Legend exports their own chats from their own phone (this is both the consent step and a technical requirement — WhatsApp only marks the exporter's messages as "You", which is what the model learns) → into data\raw\
5. Run the same 4 commands — parse → train → export → ollama create legend

Full details are in REPLICATE.md section C, inside the zip itself — so the new PC carries its own instructions, and Claude Code on that machine can read it and drive the whole setup.

⚠️ Two things to watch

- Region format: if Legend's phone exports dates as DD/MM/YYYY or 24-hour time, the parser will find 0 examples — the guide notes this, and any Claude session can adjust the regex in a minute.
- Keep private things private: the starter zip is clean, but never copy data\ or .gguf files through OneDrive/cloud — USB or local network only.

Nice milestone: your project just went from "my twin" to a reusable twin factory. 🏭

Step by step

1. Open PowerShell, enter Ubuntu:
wsl -d Ubuntu
Your prompt changes to something like root@PC:~$ — you're now in Linux. (Type exit to leave.)

2. Activate the training environment (the one setup_wsl.sh created):
source ~/twin-env/bin/activate

3. Go to the project folder — note the path translation:
cd /mnt/c/Users/jxtf9/ai-twin/training
(On the new PC, adjust to wherever the folder is, e.g. /mnt/c/Users/<name>/ai-twin/training)

4. Run the scripts:
python train_lora.py --epochs 3
python export_gguf.py

Or the one-liner shortcut (no need to "enter" WSL at all)

You can fire a WSL command straight from PowerShell — this is how I've been running them for you:
wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -c "source ~/twin-env/bin/activate; cd /mnt/c/Users/jxtf9/ai-twin/training; python train_lora.py --epochs 3"

Remember the split:
- 🐧 In WSL: train_lora.py, export_gguf.py (anything needing the training env)
- 🪟 In normal PowerShell: py scripts\parse_chats.py, ollama create, ollama run

And honestly — on the new PC, the simplest route is: install Claude Code there, open the unzipped folder, and say "read REPLICATE.md and set up the legend twin". It'll drive all of this for you like I did here.
